short: The first use of a nuclear weapon against a city, on 6 August 1945.
full:
At 8.15am on 6 August 1945 the B-29 Enola Gay released a uranium gun-type bomb, codenamed Little Boy, which detonated roughly 580 metres above Hiroshima with a yield near 15 kilotons. Around 70,000 people were killed instantly; by the end of the year the toll had risen to an estimated 140,000 from burns, injury and radiation sickness.

Nagasaki was bombed three days later, and Japan announced its surrender on 15 August. Whether the bombings were militarily necessary, given the simultaneous Soviet declaration of war, remains contested. What is not contested is their effect on everything after: the certainty that a future great-power war could end civilisation has shaped strategy, diplomacy and the imagination of every generation since.
